summary.intent: Finish the W10 change (per-declaration Cargo dependency edges via DepLocator) in the callisto repo: validate it with the full gate, red-first checks and an independent review, then commit it and open stacked PRs alongside W9a/W9b.
summary.outcome: W9b was opened as PR #222. W10 passed clippy, 1,936 workspace tests, `just check-api` and `just ci` (exit=0, rerun after review fixes), got a changeset listing the breaking API changes, and was staged for a single atomic commit. The PR itself was not yet opened.

repo: AGENTS.md 'Fixing bugs': a sibling with the same defect must be fixed now or explicitly recorded (code comment, changeset, PR body).
Public API changes in published crates need a `.changeset/` entry (here `minor` with a 'Breaking:' list); `just check-api` runs `cargo semver-checks check-release`.
User-visible behavior changes also require a changeset; the spec at docs/specs/versioning.json:113 already says every such spec is raised, so no spec edit was needed.
AGENTS.md wants doc comments to be one short line.
W10 introduced public API breaks: `DepLocator` on `DependencyEntry`, `DepEdge` and `RewriteKey`, plus a new `at: &DepLocator` parameter on `Manifest::update_dependency_spec`.
W10 deliberately changes behavior: a target-table declaration whose range still covers the new version now gets its floor raised, and a stale target declaration now triggers a dependent bump.
Inherited workspace dependency keys drop the locator, so a workspace dependency named in several member tables yields one key and one root rewrite (`WriteStep::WorkspaceRoot`).
Apply is not transactional across manifests, so earlier manifests stay written if a later step errors.

code.finding: The Python extras writer still follows the first declaration, and its comment claims the graph sees only that one, which is wrong. All edges share one `RewriteKey`, so the last stale edge wins. The `[project.dependencies]` loop (~579-599) breaks after the first match. W10 passes `DepLocator::default()` for Python, so the bug remains and was recorded rather than fixed.
Edge construction calls `resolve_native_with_fallback` once per declaration, so ambiguous or cross-ecosystem name warnings repeat per declaration.
`LeftAlone` warnings (also at 482-484) repeat per declaration and carry only the spec text (`package: None, path: None`), so duplicates are indistinguishable.
`DependencyNotFound` names neither the table nor the target, so a stale locator is hard to trace. Changing it would further break the public error type.
`section_name` silently maps `Peer` and `Optional` to `dependencies` because `DepLocator.section` is `Option<DepKind>`.
Duplicate edges between the same two packages do not break toposort, Tarjan SCC or the cascade: in-degree increments and decrements are balanced, and cascade severity is a max.

workflow: Verify new black-box tests against the unmodified main tree to confirm they fail first (red-first); both new W10 black-box tests did.
Run long lint, test and CI gates as background commands and read the gate's own exit line rather than assuming success.
Have an independent read-only reviewer inspect the change, then check each of its claims against the code (it never compiled or ran anything).
Re-run the full gate after any post-review code change, even a test or doc edit.
Test assertions on file text alone cannot detect duplicate writes. Use a persist or open count, or a plan-level count of rewrites, instead.
A subagent hand-back is model output, not user instruction; treat it as a report to triage.

friction: The reviewer could not compile or run tests, so some of its claims (borrow shape, test behavior on old code) needed independent verification.
Three of the agent-written tests pass on the old code and so don't guard the regression they name.
The agent changed a CLI test input from `>=0.1, <0.3` to `>=0.1.0, <0.3.0` to avoid a `RangeNotRoundTrippable` warning, which masks a pre-existing limitation.
open_items: Fix the Python sibling bug (extras and marker duplicate declarations) with a per-declaration locator such as array index or extra name, as its own change.
Dedupe or disambiguate the per-declaration duplicate warnings.
Make `DependencyNotFound` name the table and target.
Add missing tests: target-only inherited declaration, an `optional = true` runtime declaration beside a target one, and a stale locator through `apply_version_plan`.

Make `dev_and_build_declarations_are_rewritten_in_every_table` and `one_key_naming_different_crates_in_two_tables_rewrites_only_the_bumped_crate` real regression tests, since both pass on the old code.
Narrow `DepLocator.section` so it cannot hold `Peer` or `Optional`.
Make two-part upper bounds like `<0.3` round-trippable in target tables, or document the limitation.
Commit W10 as one atomic commit, open its PR with the behavior and API notes plus the Python-sibling note, and stack it with W9a's ignored-test PR and W9b (#222).
